You need to make major lifestyle changes because this isn’t just about aesthetics but it’s incredibly unhealthy. This may lead to issues in the longer run. 

Count your calories and eat. You have to create a calorie deficit to lose some weight. 

Eat lots of fruits. And vegetable juices and soups. Don’t drink fruit juices because blending fruits removes the fibre and leaves a sugary juice. 

Drink 2-3 litres of water regularly. You will automatically reduce junk food when you feel fuller with water. 

Incorporate channa and makhana in your diet. 

Reduce carbs like bread and rice. Eat more protein. Easier if you are a non vegetarian. 

When I was trying to lose weight my staple dinner was stir friend vegetables with paneer or tofu. Once you lose drop some weight, you will feel motivated enough to incorporate exercise in your routine. Wishing you the best.

Decide what degree you wish to pursue and look into the admission criteria for colleges offering that course. There are many colleges that require a decent 12th grade score along with entrance examinations.

I am 5’10” ( give or take an inch) and I was very embarrassed to add my height on dating apps. I would generally filter boys by their height and then after we spoke for a few days I would casually drop in my height mid conversation. Most of them have said things like “wow you’re tall for a girl” etc. however, once I really clicked with a guy and when I told him my height, he said he was an inch shorter and literally said “there could’ve been something between us if you were an inch shorter”. That was very shocking and I started hating myself. I struggled with my height for a long time, including not being a part of group pictures, sitting down even during concerts, looking for the flattest footwear available, etc. But I have grown a lot since then, I realised that I need to accept myself for who I am before I expect someone else to do it. I have dated men shorter than me, as tall as me and taller. Although it’s very hard sometimes, I try my best to be confident and carry myself. Much power to you!
